title: Vectors — 40 MCQs
description: MCQs covering distinction of scalars and vectors, addition and subtraction of coplanar vectors by scale diagrams, unit vectors, resolution into perpendicular components, component method, and scalar and vector products with applications.

questions.q: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Displacement has both magnitude and direction, so it is a vector. Mass, speed and temperature have only magnitude and are scalars.

questions.q: The physical quantity that has only magnitude but no direction is called a
questions.explanation: A scalar quantity is defined solely by its magnitude and has no associated direction.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs consists only of scalar quantities?
questions.explanation: Mass and time both have magnitude only and are scalars. The other pairs contain at least one vector.

questions.q: A unit vector is a vector whose magnitude is
questions.explanation: By definition a unit vector has magnitude exactly equal to 1 and is used to specify direction.

questions.q: The unit vector in the direction of a vector A is given by
questions.explanation: Dividing a vector by its own magnitude yields a vector of unit length pointing in the same direction.

questions.q: Two vectors of equal magnitude are inclined at 60° to each other. Their resultant has magnitude equal to
options: √3 times the magnitude of either vector
twice the magnitude of either vector
half the magnitude of either vector

questions.q: The component of a vector A along the x-axis is
questions.explanation: If θ is the angle that A makes with the positive x-axis, the x-component is A cos θ.

questions.q: The scalar product of two vectors is also known as the
questions.explanation: The scalar (or dot) product of two vectors yields a scalar quantity equal to A B cos θ.

questions.q: The vector product of two vectors is also known as the
questions.explanation: The vector (or cross) product of two vectors yields a vector perpendicular to the plane containing them.

questions.q: If two vectors are parallel, the magnitude of their cross product is
options: equal to the product of their magnitudes
equal to the sum of their magnitudes
questions.explanation: When vectors are parallel, θ = 0° or 180°, so sin θ = 0 and |A × B| = 0.

questions.q: The angle between two vectors whose resultant is maximum is
questions.explanation: Resultant R = √(A² + B² + 2AB cos θ) is maximum when cos θ = 1, i.e., θ = 0°.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct statement about unit vectors î, ĵ and k̂?
questions.explanation: By the right-hand rule, î × ĵ = k̂. Also î · ĵ = 0 and î · î = 1.

questions.q: Two forces of 5 N and 12 N act at a point. The magnitude of their resultant cannot be
questions.explanation: The resultant lies between |12 − 5| = 7 N and 12 + 5 = 17 N. Hence 5 N is impossible.

questions.q: A vector A = 3î + 4ĵ. The unit vector in the direction of A is
The angle between the vectors A = 2î + 3ĵ and B = 3î − 2ĵ is
questions.explanation: A · B = 6 − 6 = 0, therefore the vectors are perpendicular and the angle is 90°.

questions.q: If |A × B| = A · B, the angle between A and B is
questions.explanation: AB sin θ = AB cos θ ⇒ tan θ = 1 ⇒ θ = 45°.

questions.q: Three coplanar forces of magnitudes 3 N, 4 N and 5 N act on a particle. The forces can be in equilibrium if they form
questions.explanation: 3² + 4² = 5², so the forces can close to form a right-angled triangle and hence be in equilibrium.

questions.q: The component method of vector addition is preferred over the parallelogram method mainly because
options: it works only for two vectors
it can handle any number of vectors analytically
questions.explanation: Resolving into components allows algebraic addition of any number of coplanar vectors without drawing scale diagrams.

questions.explanation: By Pythagoras, other component = √(5² − 3²) = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4 m.

questions.explanation: The three equal vectors at 120° form a closed equilateral triangle, so the vector sum is zero.

The volume of the parallelepiped formed by vectors A = î + ĵ, B = ĵ + k̂ and C = k̂ + î is
questions.explanation: Volume = |A · (B × C)|. B × C = |î ĵ k̂; 0 1 1; 1 0 1| = î(1) − ĵ(−1) + k̂(−1) = î + ĵ − k̂. A · (B × C) = 1 + 1 + 0 = 2? Adjust: actually for these vectors it is 2. Correct calculation yields 2.

questions.q: A boat sails 4 km east, then 3 km north. The magnitude of its displacement from the starting point is
questions.explanation: Displacement = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √25 = 5 km (by Pythagoras).

questions.q: If A × B = C and A · B = 0, which statement is true?
options: |C| = |A| |B| and C is perpendicular to both A and B
A, B and C are coplanar and C is parallel to the plane
questions.explanation: A · B = 0 means θ = 90°, so |A × B| = AB. By definition of cross product, C is perpendicular to both A and B.
